case_name: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board and others v A. Rajappa and Others
petitioner: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board and others
facts: The case is about the definition of 'industry' under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
The Court had to interpret the meaning of 'industry' in the context of the Act.
issues: What is the meaning of 'industry' under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant argued that the definition of 'industry' should be interpreted broadly to include all types of employment.
The Court should consider the legislative history and the socioeconomic ethos of the time when interpreting the statute.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the definition of 'industry' should be interpreted narrowly to exclude certain categories of employees.
court_reasoning: The Court agreed with the approach taken by Lord Denning in Seaford Court Estates Ltd. v. Asher, [1949] 2 All. E. R. 155.
The Court considered the legislative history and the socioeconomic ethos of the time when interpreting the statute.
The Court rejected subjective notions of judges and instead looked to the words used in the statutory provision defining industry.
holding: The Court held that the definition of 'industry' should be interpreted broadly to include all types of employment, except those excluded by the Act itself.
